### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A25 and A26 each ran in every one of the 200 cases (about once per case); in the later window they are almost gone, appearing in about 5 of 200 cases (A25) and about 3 of 200 (A26). [OCC003, OCC004]
- A19 and A20 show the opposite shift: A19 is not observed earlier and A20 appears in 1 of 200 cases, while in the later window A19 runs in about 97 of 200 cases and A20 in about 102 of 200. The two are near-perfect alternatives: in about 99 of 100 later cases exactly one of them runs, and they co-occur in only about 1 of 200. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001]
- Routing around this segment is rewired. Earlier, A42's outgoing transitions went mainly to A26 (about 50 in 100) and A25 (about 44 in 100); in the later window they go to A20 (about 47 in 100) and A19 (about 44 in 100). A19 and A20, in turn, lead almost exclusively to A27 (about 97 and 96 in 100 of their outgoing transitions). [DIR006, DIR002, DIR003]
- Order relations line up with this. Earlier, A42 preceded A25 in about 99 of 100 cases and A26 in about 98 of 100, while A25 preceded A27 in about 99.5 of 100 and A26 preceded A27 in about 98.5 of 100; A25 and A26 co-occurred in every case, A25 first in about 46 of 100 and A26 first in about 53 of 100. In the later window, A42 precedes A19 in about 97 of the cases containing A19 and A20 in about 98 of the cases containing A20, and A19/A20 precede A27 in about 96–98 of those cases; A25/A26 now co-occur in only about 1 of 100 cases. [REL004, REL005, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- Distances tighten accordingly: A20 sits immediately before A27 (one event apart in about 98 of 100 later cases with the pair, against a single earlier occurrence five events apart), and the typical gap from A42 to A27 shrinks from three events (about 92 of 100 earlier) to two events (about 90 of 100 later). [LAG001, LAG002]
- A27 itself runs in every case in both windows, at a slightly earlier relative position (mean about 0.41 earlier vs about 0.39 later); A19 and A20 occupy a mean relative position of about 0.36–0.37, much where A25 sat before (about 0.37). [POS005, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- A smaller, separate shift: A14's outgoing transitions go to A15 in about 92 of 100 later cases versus about 96 before, with small new shares to A04 (about 3.5 in 100) and A02 (about 2 in 100). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the A25–A26 block, which executed between A42 and A27 in every earlier case, is replaced in the later window by exactly one activity per case — A19 in roughly half the cases and A20 in the other half — with A42 leading into it and A27 directly following. This rests on direct rather than only frequency-based signs: A42's outgoing routing moved from A25/A26 (about 94 in 100) to A19/A20 (about 91 in 100) [DIR006]; A19 and A20 route to A27 almost exclusively [DIR002, DIR003]; the order A42 → A19/A20 → A27 holds in nearly every case containing the new activities [REL004, REL005, REL008, REL009]; and the A42-to-A27 distance contracts from three events to two, consistent with one activity now sitting where two did [LAG001, LAG002]. The 31 qualifying items are many times the roughly 0.6 expected by chance in an unchanged process, so chance qualification cannot explain the pattern as a whole.

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is sampling: with 200-trace windows, variant frequencies can differ without any change, and a rare variant can appear in one window only. That explanation is strained here — a drop from 200 of 200 cases to about 4 of 200, together with directly observed rewiring at A42 and changed event distances, goes well beyond typical sampling variation — but it cannot be excluded outright. The residual later-window behaviour of A25 and A26 rests on only 5 and 3 traces [OCC003, OCC004, DIR004, DIR005], and the evidence shows nothing about what determines whether a case runs A19 rather than A20. Note also that most items describe this single segment change, so they are not independent confirmations of it.
